channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Mexican enforcer launches first in-depth market investigation
item.description: Mexico’s National Antitrust Commission has proposed sweeping legislative reforms and mandatory divestments by the country’s largest rail freight operator as part of its first-ever preliminary market investigation report.

item.title: Gender gap narrows at partner level across world’s best competition practices
item.description: The average number of women partners working within the world’s best antitrust practices increased in 2025 compared to 2024, with the number of female competition specialist associates also climbing slightly.

item.title: Smoke-filled rooms: The Tipline for 6 February 2026
item.description: Ohio attorney general David Yost has accused nine cannabis companies of illegally coordinating shelf space with one another. The Buckeye State said its consumers pay more than other parts of the US because the “cannabis cartel” allegedly conspired to eliminate local competitors and maintain high prices. item.title: Zillow defeats Compass listing challenge
item.description: Compass failed to demonstrate that Zillow is an illegal monopolist that conspired with Redfin to boycott rival real estate listings, a Manhattan federal judge has ruled in rejecting its bid for a preliminary injunction.

item.title: Cleary, Kirkland and Skadden handled toughest deals in 2025
item.description: Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton, Kirkland & Ellis and Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom represented the most companies facing in-depth merger reviews before the US antitrust agencies in 2025, according to a GCR analysis.

item.title: Record delivery: The Briefing for 9 February 2026
item.description: Chile’s competition court has approved the country’s highest antitrust fine on a single company after accepting the national competition authority’s €26.5 million settlement with Delivery Hero. The food delivery company and its subsidiary, Glovo, admitted to dividing the food delivery market in North Africa and several Latin American countries. item.title: European Commission seeks injunction in WhatsApp AI probe
item.description: The European Commission has sent Meta a formal chargesheet over its new rules banning rival AI chatbots on WhatsApp, warning that the company’s policy change appears unlawful “at first sight” and warrants an interim injunction to prevent “serious and irreparable harm”.

item.title: Hamer rejoins Baker McKenzie
item.description: Mark Hamer has stepped down as deputy assistant attorney general in the Department of Justice’s antitrust division and will return to Baker McKenzie.

item.title: Creditor pacts not subject to antitrust, lenders say
item.description: Several of the world’s largest asset managers have argued that a price-fixing suit filed by Altice USA ignores longstanding precedent that creditor agreements on debt refinancing do not violate antitrust law.

item.title: Hamer time: The Tipline for 9 February 2026
item.description: Go with the flow, it is said. Mark Hamer has left the Department of Justice’s antitrust division to return to Baker McKenzie’s antitrust partnership. The former deputy assistant attorney general said in a statement that he was “grateful” for his time and “excited to return home”. To break it down, also in Tipline, California has voted to add merger filing requirements.
